title: MoGe-3: Fine-Detail Monocular Geometry Estimation with Self-Guided Sparse Volumetric Refinement
claim: Prior methods distort and fragment thin structures in 3D reconstruction; ours preserves fine details and clean local geometry.
layout: 3x5 grid, left-to-right: input image, ours, three baselines, depth insets
description: A 3-row by 5-column grid of qualitative comparisons. The leftmost column shows the input photograph in each row: a bar table with stools, an ornate black iron gate, and a train beside a fence. The next four columns show 3D point-map renderings from Ours, MoGe-2, DA3 and InfiniDepth, with column labels under the grid. Each rendering has a small colorful depth-map inset in its top-left corner. Ours is placed right next to the input and renders thin stool legs, gate bars and fence posts as clean, continuous structures. The baselines show broken, noisy, smeared or distorted thin structures, with jagged fragments and floating points. The eye goes first to the photos, then to the contrast in thin-structure quality across the columns.
caption: Our method produces geometrically undistorted and detail-preserving metric scale point maps from a single image. Compared to prior approaches [ref], it better preserves fine structures and recovers more accurate local geometry, leading to improved 3D fidelity in challenging cases.
abstract: Monocular geometry estimation has recently achieved impressive performance across diverse scenes. However, state-of-the-art models still face notable distortion in local 3D structure, especially in fine details, like thin structures and small objects. We attribute this limitation to an architectural mismatch: most current models decode 3D geometry within a 2D parameterization, where feature interactions are governed by image-plane proximity rather than true 3D spatial relationships. This inadvertently mixes features from geometrically distant surfaces, resulting in over-smoothed geometry particularly around thin or elongated structure. In this paper, we propose MoGe-3, a fine-detail monocular geometry estimation model with Self-Guided Sparse 3D Refinement (SSR) that lifts monocular geometry modeling from 2D image space to 3D space for high-fidelity metric-scale point maps. MoGe-3 lifts the coarse point map from a foundation base model onto a sparse voxel shell and refines it via SSR. The SSR employs sparse convolutions that aggregate features based on 3D spatial locality, avoiding feature mixing across depth discontinuities. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate that MoGe-3 significantly outperforms existing approaches in recovering fine detailed 3D geometry across both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations.
